item.title: Congress Approves the Creation of the Wisconsin Territory - 97.7 Star FM
item.description: This week in Wisconsin history, the US Congress debated the boundaries and infrastructure of a new territory to be introduced to the Union. On April 20th, 1836, President Andrew Jackson approved the congressional resolution to make Wisconsin the country's newest territory. However, appointments for officials weren't made until later that July.

item.title: First Movie Projector demonstrated in US - 97.7 Star FM
item.description: On this day in US history, Woodville Latham and his sons Otway and Gray demonstrated their "Panopticon" on April 21, 1895. Inspired by the Kinetoscope, this invention would lead to the modern production of movies; there are still versions of the famous loop used in Hollywood today.

item.title: First Earth Day is Established - 97.7 Star FM
item.description: On this day in US history, the first official Earth Day was celebrated in the United States on April 22, 1970. Introduced initially by Senator Gaylord Nelson of Wisconsin, millions of Americans now celebrate the day all across the country.

item.title: US Military Academy Established - 97.7 Star FM
item.description: On this day in US history, the United States Military Academy was founded by Congress with the intention of training and educating young men in military science on March 16, 1802. item.description: On this day in US history, British forces were forced to evacuate Boston after eight years of occupation on March 17, 1776. item.description: On this day in US history, the worst tornado to ever blow through the country became the deadliest on March 18, 1925. item.description: On this day in US history, President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the Beer and Wine Revenue Act on March 22, 1933. item.description: On this day in U.S. history, the initials "O.K." were first published in The Boston Morning on March 23, 1839. At the time, it was intended as an abbreviation of "oll korrect," a popular slang misspelling of "all correct." item.title: Old Abe Dies in Fire at State Capitol - 97.7 Star FM
item.description: This week in Wisconsin history, the famous Civil War mascot for the Eau Claire infantry unit, Company C, passed away on March 26, 1881. During the Capitol fire of 1881, smoke engulfed Old Abe's cage. Only one of his feathers survived the flames; it's kept in the Wisconsin Historical Museum.

item.title: Exxon Valdez Crashes, Causing one of the Worst Oil Spills in History - 97.7 Star FM
item.description: On this day in US history, the Exxon Valdez crashed into a reef, causing one of the worst oil spills in US history on March 24, 1989. An estimated 11 million gallons of oil spilled into the Pacific Ocean, despite efforts, the contamination would spread for nearly 700 miles.

item.title: Triangle Shirtwaist fire kills 146 in New York City - 97.7 Star FM
item.description: On this day in US history, one of the darkest moments in America's industrial history occurred when the Triangle Shirtwaist Company factory caught fire on March 25, 1911. item.title: US Troops Land in Okinawa for World War Two - 97.7 Star FM
item.description: On this day in US history, after the loss of nearly 116 planes, 50,000 US troops landed on the southwest coast of Okinawa on April 1, 1945. The troops on the Japanese Island were under the command of Lieutenant General Simon Buckner Jr., who would die just three days before the Japanese surrender.
